title: Outlook on the web: inline Copilot chat for drafting emails without opening the sidebar
summary: Held because the service-desk guidance presents Copilot app access as a lever for removing the new inline chat, although that applicability remains unconfirmed. The statement that Learn gives no rollout mechanics also overlooks Microsoft's published gradual-deployment model. The roadmap facts, admin paths and audit command are supported.

claims.claim: No separate admin UI or API switch for the new Outlook web inline chat is documented as of November 2026.

claims.claim: The app block path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps. ... Select the Available Apps list. ... Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane. ... Select Block app.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The cited Integrated Apps controls are available only to Global Administrators.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.claim: Blocking the Copilot app in Integrated Apps blocks the app tenant-wide in Outlook, including licensed users.
claims.quote: If you block the Copilot app using the Integrated app control, you block the Copilot app tenant-wide across the Microsoft Copilot app, Outlook, and the web, including for users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: The Manage Copilot Chat page says the Integrated Apps block also blocks Copilot in Teams.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.
claims.fix: After this sentence add: "The Integrated Apps reference instead says blocking affects Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application, while Teams continues to honour Teams admin-center settings; the Microsoft pages disagree about Teams." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365.

claims.claim: The Copilot integrated app provides Copilot Chat in Outlook.
claims.quote: The Copilot app is an integrated app that provides Copilot Chat via web, in the Microsoft Copilot app (web, desktop, mobile) and in Outlook (web, desktop, mobile).

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: App self-installation can be scoped at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Users > Specific users/group in the organization can install.
claims.quote: Select Settings, then select Integrated Apps. ... Select the Available Apps list. ... select the app you want to edit. ... select the Users tab in the overview pane. ... Specific users/group in the organization can install

claims.claim: The specific-users/group availability option limits which users can self-install and use the app.
claims.quote: Specific users/group in the organization can install means that only the users selected by you are able to install the app on their own from the store and use it in the client. Unselected users are not able to do so.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Availability restrictions do not affect admin-deployed apps, and existing admin deployments remain honoured.
claims.quote: The availability setting of an app doesn't impact any admin deployed apps. The availability setting only allows you to control which end users can install and use these apps on their own. Any previous admin deployments made are still be honored.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends assigning only licensed users to the self-installation group to keep the Copilot app unavailable to unlicensed users.
claims.quote: select Specific users/group in the organization can install and assign a group that includes only licensed users. The app is only available to licensed users.
